attribution.note: Zitron's own unhedged sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Will have sunk' is an unqualified forecast. The proposition keeps the deadline, the $2T milestone and the returns clause. The preceding sentence identifies the four companies.

contract.note: Reading $2T as cumulative and 'very little to show' as small attributable returns is an ordinary reading. The open start date and the lack of a returns threshold are flagged. Neither matters before the deadline.

evidence.note: Amazon's own guidance of about $200B total capex for 2026. It covers one company, is total rather than AI capex, and is planned rather than realized.
Secondary roundup of the four firms' 2026 total-capex guidance ($695–725B). This is guidance for a different scope, not realized cumulative AI capex through 2027.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 2027-12-31, after the evaluation date, and no conclusive event fixes both the spending and returns clauses. The packet holds only 2026 guidance, which cannot establish realized spending. The forecast is not yet scoreable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: A present-tense observation about installation throughput, plus an inference that warehouses exist. Zitron leaves open whose warehouses they are (hyperscalers or ODMs). The proposition captures the core claim.

contract.note: Installation running at about half of shipments is the ordinary reading of 'six months per quarter'. Using Q1 2026 as the 'current' period before publication is reasonable.

evidence.note: Microsoft's disclosure that it added about 1GW of capacity in the March quarter. That is one operator's power measure, not GPU counts or an industry shipment-to-install ratio.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no matched data on GPUs shipped versus installed, and no inventory records showing accumulation beyond normal levels. One operator's capacity figure can neither confirm nor refute the claimed two-to-one ratio or the warehouses.

attribution.note: The main claim is Zitron's own. The parenthetical on Anthropic's $11B projection reports others and is not scored.

semantics.note: A loss premise plus an inference ('which means') that most AI revenue and compute depends on the two firms raising money. The causal kind fits.

contract.note: Zitron did not say whether 'lose' means net loss, operating loss or cash burn. The result on the premise turns on that unsupplied choice. The contract flags this fairly.

evidence.note: OpenAI's 2025 net loss was about $39B and its operating loss $20.9B, but the net figure includes a large one-off charge. It meets $20B on a net or operating basis and says nothing on industry dependence.

Anthropic's 2025 net loss was about $42B, mostly non-cash fair-value marks. Its operating loss was about $8B and its cash outflow about $2.6B. The quoted excerpt mainly shows 2026 half-year data. Whether it meets the threshold depends on the basis.

reviews.rationale: On net loss, both firms exceeded $20B in 2025. On operating loss or cash burn, Anthropic falls well short, so the premise turns on a basis Zitron never stated. The packet has no industry-wide revenue or compute figures and no evidence on what would happen without fundraising, so the majority-dependence conclusion is not established.

attribution.note: Zitron's own estimate from his reporting.

semantics.note: 'I estimate' is a firm quantitative claim, not a probabilistic hedge. The proposition keeps the half-quarter caveat, the $4.6B quarterly figure and the Sora 2/Codex exclusion. Context shows the figure is Azure inference spend.

contract.note: Calendar 2025, a year-end run rate and Azure inference follow from the surrounding text. The ambiguity over the annualization interval is flagged.

evidence.note: Tech Times reports $17.2B paid to Microsoft for full-year 2025, training and inference combined. That is a different scope and is not a year-end inference run rate. Part of the article relies on Zitron's own documents.

reviews.rationale: No independent Q4 or December 2025 Azure inference billing is in the packet. The full-year total of training plus inference neither confirms nor refutes a year-end inference pace above $18.5B. Zitron's own figures cannot verify themselves.
